A search over a $\delta$-net returns an $\epsilon$-optimal law over any region on which $\mu\mapsto\pi_\mu$ is Lipschitz and the chains are uniformly attracting, with explicit constants and, on an interval, an explicit sample size. Under contraction on average, $\mu\mapsto\pi_\mu$ is differentiable, its derivative is injective if and only if the push-forwards $(w_i)_\#\pi_\mu$ are linearly independent, and the objective is weakly convex, so that a projected subgradient method with inexact subgradients converges to near-stationary points.
item.dc:creator: Allahkaram Shafiei, Robert Shorten, Jakub Marecek

item.title: Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.34289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Pr\'ekopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincar\'e inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincar\'e-type inequality associated with smooth norms.
item.dc:creator: Dario Cordero-Erausquin, Galyna V. Livshyts, Liran Rotem

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Roshka

item.title: Online Discrepancy of Sparse Random Vectors over Long Horizons
item.description: arXiv:2610.34410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=\Theta(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time. Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $\Omega(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{\alpha_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $\alpha_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$. The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.34433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.
item.dc:creator: Yunus Alp Biyikoglu, R. Srikant

item.title: On maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.34443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs, in which a group of vertices succeeds with a probability that depends on the sum of its members' parameters. The data are independent binary outcomes of experiments on groups of vertices, tested according to an arbitrary, possibly incomplete design. Suppose that every tested group has $k$ vertices and success probability in $[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]$. For complete designs in which every group is tested at least $r$ times, a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) exists with high probability if $r\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}\log n/n^{k-1}$, and for $m$ experiments on uniformly random groups, it suffices that $m\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}n\log n$, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. Both conditions are linear in $\epsilon^{-1}$ and, for fixed $k$, cannot be improved in general beyond the constant; they follow from finite-sample bounds for arbitrary designs. We bound the mean squared error of the MLE over a parameter box by the smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the design, and show that the rate is minimax optimal for balanced complete designs. Among $k$-uniform designs with a given number of experiments, designs in which every pair of vertices takes part together in the same number of experiments maximize this eigenvalue, and uniform random designs nearly do so with high probability. Finally, the design matrix of a uniform random design has full column rank with high probability if $m\geq\max\{n,c(n/k)\log n\}$ for fixed $c>2$ and $k=o(n/\log n)$, or $m\geq n$ when $k\geq(1+\xi)\log n$. For fixed $k$, the threshold $(n/k)\log n$ is sharp, and above it rank deficiency is asymptotically as likely as some vertex taking part in no experiment.
item.dc:creator: Milan Vojnovi\'c, Yiliu Wang

item.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
item.description: arXiv:2610.34583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a deceptively hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients flatten, turbulence makes the signal intermittent, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate enemy armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. An exact confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether to keep searching for the plume source or land. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.
item.dc:creator: Kordel Kade France

item.title: Beyond Deduplication: Sharp Retrieval Limits for Attention with Correlated Distractors
item.description: arXiv:2610.34682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Redundant context affects attention through two distinct mechanisms: repeated items add normalization mass, while score variation within correlated groups can produce extreme individual scores. We separate these effects in a planted retrieval model with exponentially many Gaussian distractors arranged in known, exponentially large clusters. The model is a two-level generalized random energy model, whose classical free energy yields exact retrieval thresholds. Gaussian interpolation further shows that increasing positive correlation at fixed token count lowers the distractor free energy, unlike adding duplicates. Our main result identifies a sharp limitation of subtracting log cluster size from pre-softmax scores: this correction removes multiplicity but retains within-cluster extremes. Even a temperature chosen after observing all scores cannot lower the required signal below $\sqrt{2\alpha_1}$, where $\alpha_1$ is the exponential rate of the number of clusters. Averaging scores before exponentiation instead suppresses these fluctuations and achieves $\sqrt{2\rho\alpha_1}$, where $\rho$ is the within-cluster correlation. The gap persists after adding exponentially many singleton distractors, so group size alone does not identify the target, and extends to fixed finite hierarchies of light-tailed independent-increment scores. Finite-sample, stability, and participation results complement the asymptotic analysis. A controlled retrieval experiment with frozen sentence embeddings supports this distinction while delineating its scope: averaging helps when the relevant item is a singleton, but can discard useful evidence when a relevant group contains multiple matching items.
item.dc:creator: Heehyun Park

item.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
item.description: arXiv:2610.34750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Poisson approximation theorem states that when $m$ balls are tossed uniformly and randomly into $n$ bins, the distribution of the bin loads can sometimes be approximated by $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. We show that when the balls are tossed via a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map, the load distribution is still governed by this Poisson distribution, albeit in a (necessarily) weaker manner. This allows us to show that a random linear map behaves like a fully random map in the following ways: 1. $\textbf{Expected loads.}$ We show that the expected value of the $r$th largest bin is governed by the $r$th largest value among $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. Specializing to the canonical setting of $m=n$ and $r=1$, our bounds show that the expected maximum load when $n$ balls are hashed into $n$ bins by a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map is no more than the corresponding expectation for a fully random map $\textit{plus}$ $\frac{3}2 + o(1)$. Specializing to $m\gg n\log n$, we show that the expected max load is $(1+o(1))m/n$ in this regime. 2. $\textbf{Concentration.}$ When $m\gg n\log (1/\rho)$ balls are tossed into $n$ bins randomly, we expect with $0.99$ probability that $\textit{every}$ density-$\rho$ subset of bins will contain a $(1\pm o(1) )\rho$-fraction of the balls. We show that this remains the case if the $m$ balls are tossed using a random linear map, and our bound matches the $o(1)$-factor produced by the fully random case. This gives a stronger version of the Leftover Hash Lemma for linear maps. An implication of this is that all bins have load $m/n \pm O(\sqrt{(m/n)\log n})$ with probability $0.99$. We obtain these results by showing that the average of a log-potential on the bin loads is upper bounded by the cumulant generating function of a Poisson random variable of mean $m/n$.
item.dc:creator: Vinayak M. Kumar

item.title: Covariance spectra of random linear systems near instability
item.description: arXiv:2610.34920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how stationary variance is distributed among the principal components of a randomly coupled linear system near instability. The coupling matrix has entries $N^{-1/2}\xi_{ij}$, where the $\xi_{ij}$ are independent copies of a bounded, centered real random variable of variance one. As $N\to\infty$ and the excess damping $\delta_N\to0$, we prove that the covariance spectrum, with eigenvalues rescaled by $\delta_N^2$ and weighted by their shares of the total variance, converges in probability to an explicit beta-product law. The convergence holds throughout $\delta_N\ge N^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$ for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. The law describes eigenvalues of order $\delta_N^{-2}$ at ranks of order $N\delta_N^{3/2}$. Its limiting rank profile decays as $r^{-4/3}$ at large normalized rank and determines how many principal components retain a prescribed fraction of the stationary variance. The proof combines an exact computation of planar moments, uniform estimates for growing matrix words that accommodate nonsymmetric entry distributions, and resolvent bounds controlling the contribution of long times.
item.dc:creator: Pengbin Feng

item.title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.35022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Sotnikov, Adeline Viot

item.title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.35352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Stochastic Transport in Upper Ocean Dynamics project introduced a new paradigm for representing uncertainty in geophysical fluid dynamics through stochastic transport models calibrated from data. This paper provides a synthesis of the principal theoretical and data assimilation developments achieved as part of the project. The central theme of the paper is the transformation of stochastic transport models from a modelling paradigm into a mathematically rigorous framework equipped with analytical, variational, calibration and Bayesian data assimilation methodologies suitable for geophysical fluid dynamics. We describe the development of the theory of stochastic transport equations, including well-posedness, regularity and approximation results, together with their geometric foundations based on stochastic variational principles, rough paths and fractional transport models. We further review methodologies for calibrating stochastic transport structures from observational and high-resolution simulation data, ranging from reduced-order stochastic models to modern generative approaches. Finally, we discuss Bayesian inference and high-dimensional data assimilation techniques developed for stochastic transport models, including particle filter methodologies and machine learning uncertainty quantification. Taken together, these developments establish a coherent framework linking stochastic transport modelling, rigorous analysis, calibration and Bayesian inference, thereby providing a foundation for uncertainty quantification and forecasting in geophysical fluid dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Dan Crisan, Oana Lang

item.title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
item.description: arXiv:2610.35759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<\beta<4\pi$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li, Jianfeng Lu

item.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.35760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,\theta}$ boundary, $0<\theta\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: Quantum dynamics on the sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.35867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyse the large-time asymptotics of the Schr\"odinger time evolution of a free quantum particle on the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(N,d/N)$, where the quantum Hamiltonian is given by the adjacency matrix of $\mathbb{G}$. Starting from a state localized at a vertex, the wave function is approximately radial, and we characterize precisely its asymptotic form. Our results in particular cover vertices whose degree is close to $2d$, hence probing the emergence of bound states from a dynamical perspective. This provides a dynamical counterpart of the coexistence of localized and delocalized states established in [arXiv:1905.03243,arXiv:2005.14180,arXiv:2106.12519,arXiv:2109.03227,arXiv:2305.16294], with the former giving rise to a localized mode and the latter to a dispersive wave. Our results hold in the regime $\sqrt{\log N} \ll d \ll N^{o(1)}$, which is the full region in which such dynamical phenomena may exist, and for times $1 \ll t \ll T_N$ for some explicit $T_N \gg 1$.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Alt, Raphael Ducatez, Antti Knowles

item.title: An Abstract Framework for Nonlinear Stochastic Parabolic Systems with Application to a Chemotaxis-Fluid Model
item.description: arXiv:2401.17668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of the paper is twofold. Firstly, we want to present an abstract existence Theorem to show the existence of a martingale solution for coupled systems of non-linear stochastic partial differential equations. The idea is first to split the system by rewriting the nonlinear part in a linear part acting on a given process. This is done in such a way that the fixed point with respect to the given process would be the solution of the original Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE). However, it may be necessary to show the well-posedness of the linearized system using a cut-off argument, which may impose additional constraints. We work out under which conditions on the underlying spaces and the cut-off argument one gets a martingale solution of the original SPDE. A similar strategy was applied by Hausenblas and Tolle in [E. Hausenblas and J. Tolle. The stochastic Klausmeier system and a schauder tychonoff type theorem. Potential Analusis, 310:506-554, 2022] to investigate the stochastic Klausmeier system. Secondly, we want to verify the full applicability of the existence Theorem by showing the existence of a martingale solution of a highly nonlinear chemotaxis system with underlying fluid dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Erika Hausenblas, Boris Jidjou Moghomye

item.title: Hitting probability for Reflected Brownian Motion at Small Target
item.description: arXiv:2402.00997v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the asymptotic behavior of hitting probability at small target of size $O(\epsilon)$ for reflected Brownian motion in domains with suitable smooth boundary conditions, where the boundary of domain contains both reflecting part, absorbing part and target. In this case the domain could be localized near the target and explicit computations are possible. The asymptotic behavior is only related to $\epsilon$ up to some multiplicative constants that depends on the domain and boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Fan

item.title: Velocity surface disorder of large deviation rates for high-dimensional random walk in strongly mixing environment
item.description: arXiv:2409.06581v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we establish the large deviation principles of random walk in strongly mixing environments. We show that the quenched and annealed rate functions share the same zero-set whose shape is either a singleton point or a line segment, with an illustrative example communicated and given by F. Rassoul-Agha. Furthermore, this paper reveals that under sufficiently low disorder, the two rate functions match on compact sets of both the interior and the boundary of the domain under finitely strongly mixing condition.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Chen

item.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2412.15969v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi

item.title: The Integrable Snake Model
item.description: arXiv:2501.15483v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A pure snake configuration is a bijection $\sigma:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing no two-cycles and such that for each $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ we have $\sigma(x) \in \{ x , x+ \mathbf{e}^1, x+\mathbf{e}^2 , x- \mathbf{e}^2 \}.$ The non-trivial cycles of a pure snake configuration may be regarded as a collection of non-intersecting paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that may travel right, up, or down (but not left) from a given vertex. Pure snake configurations are a generalisation of lozenge tilings, which are in natural correspondence with paths that only travel right or up. We introduce a partition function on a finite version of this model and study the probabilistic properties of random pure snake configurations chosen according to their contribution to this partition function. Under a suitable weighting, the model is integrable in the sense that we have access to explicit formulas for its partition function and correlation function. We utilise the integrable structure of this model in several applications through its various scaling limits, such as to prove a traffic representation of ASEP on the ring, generalising the analogous result for TASEP by the first author.
item.dc:creator: Samuel G. G. Johnston, Rohan Shiatis

item.title: Heavy-tailed random vectros: theory and applications
item.description: arXiv:2503.12842v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we introduce and study several multivariate, heavy-tailed distribution classes, and we explore their closure properties and their applications. We consider the class of multivariate positively decreasing distributions, and its intersection with other multivariate distribution classes.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios G. Konstantinides, Charalampos D. Passalidis

item.title: Spectra of contractions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Tensor Ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2505.10555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the spectra of matrix-valued contractions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Tensor Ensemble (GOTE). Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote a random tensor of order $r$ and dimension $n$ drawn from the density \[ f(\mathcal{G}) \propto \exp\bigg(-\frac{1}{2r}\|\mathcal{G}\|^2_{\mathrm{F}}\bigg). \] For $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{S}^{n - 1}$, the unit-sphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we consider the matrix-valued contraction $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{w}^{\otimes (r - 2)}$ when both $r$ and $n$ go to infinity such that $r / n \to c \in [0, \infty]$. We obtain semicircle bulk-limits in all regimes, generalising the works of Goulart et al. (2022); Au and Garza-Vargas (2023); Bonnin (2024) in the fixed-$r$ setting. We further study the edge-spectrum. We obtain a Baik-Ben Arous-P\'{e}ch\'{e} phase-transition for the largest and the smallest eigenvalues at $r \ge 4$, generalising a result of Mukherjee et al. (2024) in the context of adjacency matrices of random hypergraphs. For $r = 3$, the fluctuations of the extreme eigenvalues are given by the eigenvalues of a stochastic Airy operator, whereas for $r \ge 4$, the fluctuations are Gaussian. Finally, we report some results, in the case $r = 4$, on mixed contractions $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n - 1}$. While the total variation distance between the joint distributions of the entries of $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$ and $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{u}$ goes to $0$ when $\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}\| = o(n^{-1})$, the bulk and the largest eigenvalues of these two matrices share the same limit profile as long as $\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}\| = o(1)$. Furthermore, it turns out that there are no outlier eigenvalues in the spectrum of $\mathcal{G} \cdot \mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v}$ when $\langle \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \rangle = o(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Soumendu Sundar Mukherjee, Himasish Talukdar

item.title: Functional second-order Gaussian Poincar\'e inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2506.13571v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we work in the framework of Hilbert-valued Wiener structures and derive a functional version of the second-order Gaussian Poincar\'e inequality that leads to abstract bounds for Gaussian process approximation in $d_2$ distance used by Bourguin and Campese (Electron. J. Probab., 2020). As pointed out by Bassetti, Bourguin, Campese, and Peccati (Statist. Probab. Lett., 2026) this distance alone does not imply weak convergence in infinite dimensions, we also consider $d_2^\dagger$, obtained by adding the absolute difference of the second moments. This metric metrizes $2$-Wasserstein convergence and agrees with $d_2$ for centered variables with matching covariance operators. Our abstract bounds are flexible and can be applied in various examples including functional Breuer-Major central limit theorems, shallow neural networks, and spatial statistics of SPDE solutions. In these applications, the covariance estimates also give the second-moment convergence needed for weak convergence in the corresponding Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Anna Vidotto, Guangqu Zheng

item.title: Crossings and diffusion in Poisson driven marked random connection models
item.description: arXiv:2507.03965v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We first study crossing statistics in random connection models (RCM) built on marked Poisson point processes on $\mathbb R^d$. Under general assumptions, we show exponential tail bounds for the number of crossings of a box contained in the infinite cluster for supercritical intensity of the point process, and percolation in slabs, in analogy with the Grimmett-Marstrand theorem. We then present several applications to transport and diffusion phenomena. In particular, we prove the non-degeneracy of the effective homogenized matrix arising in the large-scale limit of random walks, exclusion processes, and resistor networks on the RCM, and the non-degeneracy of the effective diffusion constant for one-dimensional diffusion operators on the Euclidean graph associated with the RCM. As examples, we apply our results to Poisson-Boolean models and Mott variable range hopping random resistor network, providing a fundamental ingredient used in the derivation of Mott's law.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Faggionato, Ivailo Hartarsky

item.title: Inhomogeneous branching trees with symmetric and asymmetric offspring and their genealogies
item.description: arXiv:2510.07921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define symmetric and asymmetric branching trees, a class of processes particularly suited for modeling genealogies of inhomogeneous populations where individuals may reproduce throughout life. In this framework, a broad class of Crump-Mode-Jagers processes can be constructed as (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which count the branches of the tree. Analogous definitions yield reduced (a)symmetric Sevast'yanov processes, which restrict attention to branches that lead to extant progeny. We characterize their laws through generating functions. The genealogy obtained by pruning away branches without extant progeny at a fixed time is shown to satisfy a branching property, which provides distributional characterizations of the genealogy.
item.dc:creator: Frederik M. Andersen, Marc A. Suchard, Carsten Wiuf, Samir Bhatt

item.title: Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.09930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the martingale dimension of diffusion processes associated with strongly local regular Dirichlet forms on metric measure spaces. The martingale dimension is an intrinsic quantity describing the probabilistic complexity of a diffusion, but its precise determination in non-smooth settings is highly nontrivial. In this paper, we establish a purely analytic criterion, formulated in terms of energy measures and relative capacities, which guarantees that the AF-martingale dimension equals one. Our approach does not rely on self-similarity, heat kernel estimates, or global geometric assumptions, and applies to settings where such structures are unavailable. The proof is based on a blow-up analysis of harmonic functions combined with a push-forward argument for energy measures, which excludes the coexistence of multiple independent martingale directions. As applications, we verify the assumptions of the theory for a class of inhomogeneous Sierpinski gaskets, including genuinely non-self-similar examples, and for the two-dimensional standard Sierpinski carpet, where the criterion yields a new capacity-based proof of the one-dimensionality of the martingale structure. In these examples, self-similarity or local symmetry enters only in verifying the hypotheses; the mechanism that forces the one-dimensionality is the analytic balance condition itself.
item.dc:creator: Masanori Hino

item.title: Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model
item.description: arXiv:2603.26936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using sharp global heat kernel bounds and geodesic comparison geometry, we show that the Dalang condition for well-posedness of the parabolic Anderson model with measure-valued initial conditions, first introduced on Euclidean space, holds on general compact Riemannian manifolds. We furthermore establish upper and lower moment bounds for all such solutions, providing evidence for intermittency in this generality. This extends and simplifies earlier work that required non-positive curvature.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Chen, Robert Neel, Cheng Ouyang

item.title: Quasihelix properties of selected Volterra Gaussian processes
item.description: arXiv:2605.20026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study local quasihelix and generalized quasihelix properties of several Gaussian Volterra processes with tempered, power-weighted, and logarithmic kernels, including tempered fractional Brownian motions and generalized fractional Brownian motion-type processes. These properties depend significantly on the values of the parameters involved, and we consider all possible cases in detail.
item.dc:creator: Yuliya Mishura, Kostiantyn Ralchenko

item.title: Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2605.30560v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unlike classical optimal transport, weak transport costs depend nonlinearly on the conditional law of couplings. This feature is essential in problems involving barycenter, conditional moments, and martingale-type constraints. Meanwhile, such conditional dependence makes ordinary Wasserstein geometry insufficient and calls instead for an adapted Wasserstein viewpoint. In this paper, we investigate the entropy-regularized weak optimal transport via gradient flows in adapted Wasserstein space. We derive, from the formal tangent structure of adapted Wasserstein space and the projection onto the set of couplings with prescribed marginals, a coupled McKean--Vlasov SDE. A novel and subtle term is a projection that, at each $Y$-location, averages a weak-transport force that already depends on the conditional law of $Y$ given $X$, thereby preserving marginals while retaining the nonlinear weak-transport structure. Under mild integrability and regularity assumptions, we prove weak existence and uniqueness in law for this projected McKean--Vlasov equation. We then prove that the flow converges, in the adapted Wasserstein topology, to the unique minimizer of the entropic weak optimal transport problem. We also describe a particle approximation and illustrate the dynamics on optimal transport and martingale optimal transport examples.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Sauldubois, Xin Zhang

item.title: The conditional expectation of the product of the first $n-1$ Hermite polynomials in a multivariate normal distribution with respect to the $n$-th variable. A fresh perspective on the Kibble-Slepian formula
item.description: arXiv:2606.22526v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the conditional expectation of $\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}H_{k_{j}}% (X_{j})$ given $X_{n}=z,$ if random vector $(X_{1},\ldots,X_{n})^{T}$ has multivariate normal distribution and $H_{n}(x)$ denotes $n$-th Hermite polynomial. This expectation is a polynomial in $z$ of order $\sum_{j=1}% ^{n-1}k_{j}$. Our formula has an iterative form with respect to $n$. We also present some auxiliary observations concerning the expansion of the density of the $n$-dimensional normal distribution in the series of the Hermite polynomials. Mostly concerning the properties of the coefficients of this expansion. To perform these calculations, we give a few auxiliary formulas concerning Hermite polynomials and multivariate normal distributions. We apply this result to obtain exact, simple forms of these expansions for $n=2$ and $3$, thus looking at known results from a different perspective. We believe that the results can be very useful in Probability Theory, in particular in the Theory of distributions, Statistics, and the Theory of Stochastic Processes, in particular Gaussian ones.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} J. Szab{\l}owski

item.title: Matrix-analytic methods for $M/M_D/c$ queues with Marshall--Olkin dependent servers
item.description: arXiv:2606.24881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study multiserver queues with Marshall--Olkin dependent service mechanisms, heterogeneous servers, and fixed idle-set assignment. An explicit matrix-analytic solution links the stationary queue distribution to departure and customer-delay laws. Waiting time conditional on delay is exactly exponential, and the stationary \chg{sojourn law has a phase-type representation with at most one more phase than the number of servers.} A consistency condition characterizes when Markovian completions admit a Poisson shock representation. For two three-server families with identical bivariate residual-service laws, we prove a conditional waiting-time ordering and identify when their unconditional waiting tails cross. The results show how higher-order dependence affects performance beyond marginal rates and pairwise service dependence.
item.dc:creator: Qihui Bu, Suman Thapa, Yiqiang Q. Zhao

item.title: Strong convergence of Euler-Maruyama schemes for additive fractional SDEs with Lipschitz drift
item.description: arXiv:2607.24166v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the strong convergence rate of the Euler--Maruyama scheme for additive stochastic differential equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$. Assuming the drift coefficient to be Lipschitz continuous, we establish strong convergence bounds of order $1$ if $H\in(1/2,1)$, and $1/2+H-\varepsilon$, for any $\varepsilon>0$, if $H\in(0,1/2]$. The main ingredient is a shifted stochastic sewing argument, which exploits the conditional Gaussian structure of fractional Brownian motion to control the noise discretization error.
item.dc:creator: Tsukasa Moritoki

item.title: Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles
item.description: arXiv:2609.02257v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove uniform endpoint estimates, killed local limits, and conditioned-bridge invariance principles for triangular arrays of centered, aperiodic, integer-valued random walks with uniform exponential tails. The endpoint estimates cover all nonnegative heights, while the local limits treat positive diffusive and zero endpoints. The increment law may vary with the scaling parameter.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Xu

item.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
item.description: arXiv:2609.03532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $\beta>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $\beta$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_\beta$ process for $\beta\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $\beta$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $\beta=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Xu

item.title: Mixing time under monotone censoring
item.description: arXiv:2609.16515v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Ding and Mossel~\cite{DM}: the lazy random walk on the discrete cube, censored to any increasing set of fixed positive density, mixes in time $O(n\log n)$. More precisely, for every nonempty increasing set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, with $a=\mu(A)$ and $\mu$ uniform on the cube, we prove $$ t_{\mathrm{mix}}(P)\le C_a n\log(en), $$ where $C_a$ depends only on $a$. The proof uses hypercontractivity on the ambient cube to strengthen the Poincar\'e inequality on coordinate sections. An optimal stopping time occupation inequality for increasing sets converts the resulting local bound into a uniform bound on hitting times of large sets. An appendix by Y.~Peres improves the density dependence to $C_a=13a^{-1}\log(e/a)$, within a logarithmic factor of the conjectured $a^{-1}$ dependence.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Chen, Yuval Peres

item.title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
item.description: arXiv:2609.35383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--P\'olya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Sadat Mirsajjadi

item.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
item.description: arXiv:2610.09258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=\tau\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $\tau\lambda_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $\lambda_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $\Delta\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $\delta>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Backward stochastic partial differential equations with unbounded random coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.09278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a linear backward stochastic partial differential equation with unbounded observation-adapted random coefficients, motivated by the duality approach to nonlinear filtering. The coefficients depend predictably on the observation history through a control with almost surely finite time-integrated squared norm. The drift, diffusion, and coefficient multiplying the martingale integrand may grow linearly in space. The diffusion matrix may grow quadratically in space and is allowed to be degenerate. Under bounded positive-order spatial derivatives and bounded smooth observation-measurable terminal data, we prove existence and uniqueness in a polynomially weighted Sobolev class up to control-energy stopping times. The proof combines conditional parameter estimates, entropy bounds for likelihoods, stability under the reference probability, and stochastic-flow reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Jie Xiong, Wen Xu, Zuo Quan Xu, Ying Yang

item.title: Limit shapes for centrally excited walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.10162v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A centrally excited random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$ moves like simple random walk, except that its first step from each site other than the origin has a drift of fixed size toward it. Kozma (2007) conjectured that after $n$ steps the visited set approximates a ball with radius of order $n^{1/(d+1)}$. We prove this in every dimension $d\geq 2$ and show that the rescaled local times converge uniformly to a cone, which is the potential generated by the drift on a ball. The same argument shows that, when the drift is opposite to a subgradient of a norm, the visited set approximates the ball of that norm. In the plane, the outer and inner radii of the visited set differ by at most $n^{1/6}$ times a power of $\log n$, and the exponent $1/6$ cannot be lowered. Earlier versions of this work appeared in three independent drafts by Nguyen (arXiv:2610.07724), Bou-Rabee and Peres (arxiv:2610.10162v1) and Singh (arxiv:2610.12138). The present paper brings together the results and ideas from these drafts.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Yuval Peres, Arvind Singh

item.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Chiclana

item.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
item.description: arXiv:2610.17307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) \zeta_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $\zeta$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{\alpha-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Pr\"omel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $\zeta = dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
item.dc:creator: Tim Van Hoose

item.title: Enhanced Dissipation by Transport Noise for Stochastic $p(x)$-Laplace Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We are concerned with dissipation enhancement by divergence-free transport noise for stochastic \(p(x)\)-Laplace equations on \(\mathbb T^d\), \(d\ge2\). Spatially variable growth removes homogeneous scaling and produces two flux growth regimes. For periodic log-H\"older continuous exponents satisfying \(2<p^-\le p^+<\infty\), we first establish global variational well-posedness and the exact energy identity in the natural dual spaces. Under the additional condition \(p^+<2d/(d-2)\) when \(d\ge3\), we then prove averaged algebraic decay with any prescribed coefficient, uniformly on bounded zero-mean \(L^2\) balls, by estimating the two flux powers separately. A deterministic lower bound yields strict averaged comparison with the unperturbed flow at prescribed positive times on shells with bounded gradient modular. We also prove optimality of the modular coercivity exponent \(p^+\) near zero. Finally, combining these estimates with intervalwise noise acceleration from the constant-exponent theory gives exponential decay in mean square and almost surely, with moments of the random prefactors bounded uniformly on the initial-data ball. For the exponential estimates, the noise depends on the prescribed rate and moment order; its intensity is fixed in time and its frequency range increases.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwei Zhang, Juntao Wu, Shang Wu

item.title: Normal approximation, moderate and large deviations for the elephant random walk with stops and random step sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the elephant random walk with stops and independent positive random step sizes. Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cram\'er-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Liang

item.title: Compatibility-based Bayesian inference: asymptotic limits, variational principles, and Wasserstein geometry
item.description: arXiv:2105.01962v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) replaces intractable likelihood evaluations with comparisons between observed and simulated data. We formulate discrepancy-based inference through nonnegative compatibility weights. Prior-integrated convergence of rescaled weights gives total variation convergence as the tolerance vanishes. For a fixed positive tolerance and increasing sample size, we give a general representation-based formulation of the conditional-prior limit known from ABC and coarsened Bayesian inference, and establish convergence in expected total variation under stabilization in probability and a prior-null boundary condition. We also derive acceptance-persistence bounds under partial stabilization. The Gibbs variational identity yields convergence of minimum values and stability of approximate minimizers; the fixed-tolerance limit is characterized separately by constrained relative-entropy minimization. For additional penalty-based functionals of the limiting Wasserstein discrepancy, we prove an exact reduction to distributions over model laws and, under a geodesic assumption, a representation by distances from a Wasserstein ball. These penalty-based updates are distinguished from the original fixed-tolerance ABC limit and illustrated through a Gaussian comparison.
item.dc:creator: Marco Tarsia, Antonietta Mira, Daniele Cassani

item.title: A multistate approach to disability insurance reserving with information delays
item.description: arXiv:2312.14324v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Disability insurance claims are often affected by lengthy reporting delays and adjudication processes. The classic multistate life insurance modeling framework is ill-suited to handle such information delays since the cash flow and available information can no longer be based on the biometric multistate process determining the contractual payments. We propose a new individual reserving model for disability insurance schemes which describes the claim evolution in real-time. Under suitable independence assumptions between the available information and the underlying biometric multistate process, we show that these new reserves may be calculated as natural modifications of the classic reserves. For estimation of the model constituents, we employ the procedure proposed in [Buchardt, K., Furrer, C., & Sandqvist, O. L. (2025). Estimation for multistate models subject to reporting delays and incomplete event adjudication. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 19(4), 2782-2802. https://doi.org/10.1214/25-AOAS2068]. A real data application illustrates how the proposed estimation and reserving methods can be implemented and compares the resulting reserves with simpler reserving approaches.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Lunding Sandqvist

item.title: Characters of symmetric groups: sharp bounds on virtual degrees and the Witten zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2411.04347v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the virtual degrees introduced by Larsen and Shalev. This leads to improved bounds on characters of symmetric groups. We then sharpen bounds of Liebeck and Shalev concerning the Witten zeta function. Our main application is a characterization of the fixed-point free conjugacy classes whose associated random walk mixes in 2 steps.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Teyssier, Paul Th\'evenin

item.title: Optimal regret for dynamic matching with static priorities
item.description: arXiv:2503.09762v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study centralized two-way dynamic matching markets in which agents arrive stochastically over time and wait in queues associated with their types. We focus on static priority policies that assign each agent type a fixed ranking over its neighbors and make online matching decisions using only queue availability. We propose the General Priority ($\mathbf{GP}$) policy, which builds on the Tree Priority ($\mathbf{TP}$) policy introduced in [KAG25]. Under the general position gap condition, $\mathbf{GP}$ selects matches using a nondegenerate optimal basic solution of the fluid relaxation. It prioritizes children over parents within trees and consistently gives clockwise neighbors priority over counterclockwise neighbors on each cycle. We establish the optimal all-time regret scaling $O(\epsilon^{-1})$ for $\mathbf{GP}$ on general two-way matching networks, where the general position gap $\epsilon$ measures the fluid relaxation's distance from degeneracy. In particular, this resolves the conjecture by [KAG25] on the optimal $\epsilon$-dependence for $\mathbf{TP}$.
item.dc:creator: S\"uleyman Kerimov, Pengyu Qian, Mingwei Yang, Sophie H. Yu

item.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
item.description: arXiv:2503.11770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi, Nikita Simonov

item.title: Case Studies in Generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein Duality
item.description: arXiv:2510.23552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality guarantees coincidence between metrics on the space of probability distributions defined on the one hand via transport plans (couplings) and on the other hand via price functions. Both constructions have been lifted to the level of generality of set functors, with the construction based on couplings referred to as the Wasserstein or simply the coupling-based lifting, and the price-function-based construction as the Kantorovich or codensity lifting, both based on a choice of quantitative modalities for the given functor. It is known that every coupling-based lifting can be expressed as a price-function-based lifting; however, the latter in general needs to use additional modalities. We give an example showing that this cannot be avoided in general. We refer to cases in which the same modalities can be used as satisfying the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality. We establish the generalized Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality in this sense for two important cases: The L\'evy-Prokhorov distance on distributions, which finds wide-spread applications in machine learning due to its favourable stability properties, and the standard metric on convex sets of distributions that arises by combining the Hausdorff and Kantorovich-Rubinstein distances. Furthermore we generalize (coupling-based) functor liftings from set functors to functors which act on (pseudo-)metric spaces, thus incorporating new example functors that map to closed subsets respectively Radon measures.
item.dc:creator: Paul Wild, Lutz Schr\"oder, Pedro Nora, Barbara K\"onig, Jonas Forster

item.title: Structured Continuity Equations in Fibred Wasserstein Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.19784v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we develop a comprehensive ODE-theory for structured continuity equations in fibred probability spaces, which represent a class of heterogeneous PDEs arising as the meanfield limit of nonexchangeable particle systems. After investigating in depth the topologies induced by the so-called fibred (or conditional) and classical Wasserstein metrics on such probability spaces, we establish quantitative Cauchy-Lipschitz and qualitative Carath\'eodory-Peano well-posedness results for structured continuity equations, along with precise correspondences between this class of evolutions, classical Lagrangian dynamics, and continuity equations. In keeping with what has long been known for exchangeable dynamics, we derive a general meanfield approximation result by solutions of nonexchangeable particle systems, along with a quantitative variant thereof under practically reasonable regularity assumptions on the driving field and initial data.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Bonnet-Weill, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil

item.title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
item.description: arXiv:2512.14190v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and L\'evy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fr\'echet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Goria, Levent A. Meng\"ut\"urk, Murat C. Meng\"ut\"urk, Berkan Sesen

item.title: The Radon--Nikodym topography of acyclic measured graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.24741v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Adams dichotomy [Ada90] characterizes amenability of probability-measure-preserving treed equivalence relations in terms of the ends of a given treeing. We extend this dichotomy to the measure-class-preserving (mcp) setting by analyzing the Radon--Nikodym topography of an acyclic mcp Borel graph, i.e., the interaction between the graph geometry and the associated Radon--Nikodym cocycle. In the general mcp setting one must count not all ends, but only the nonvanishing ends: those ends which have positive upper cocycle-weight. More precisely, we prove that a locally countable acyclic mcp graph is amenable if and only if a.e. component has at most two nonvanishing ends, while it is nowhere amenable exactly when a.e. component has a nonempty perfect closed set of nonvanishing ends. At the heart of our analysis lies the study of acyclic countable-to-one Borel functions. Our critical result is that, outside of the essentially two-ended setting, all back ends in a.e. orbit are vanishing and have cocycle-finite geodesics. We also give several characterizations, including topographical and cocycle-free, of essential one-endedness of such functions, and show that the number of barytropic ends controls the essential number of ends. Our proofs utilize mass transport, end selection, and the notion of the Radon--Nikodym core for acyclic mcp graphs, a new concept that serves as a guiding framework for our topographical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob

item.title: Improved well-posedness for the limit flow of differentiation of roots of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2602.06826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the partial differential equation on the circle that was heuristically obtained by Steinerberger \cite{steinerberger2019nonlocal} on the real line and which represents the evolution of the density of the roots of polynomials under differentiation. After integrating the partial differential equation in question, we observe that it can be treated with the theory of viscosity solutions. This equation at hand is a non linear parabolic integro-differential equation which involves the elliptic operator called the half-Laplacian. Due to the singularity of the equation, we first restrict our study to strictly positive initial condition. We obtain a comparison principle for solutions of the primitive equation which yields uniqueness, existence, continuity with respect to initial condition. We then extend these results to general initial data. We finally prove that the system of particles on the circle introduced by Steinerberger indeed approximates the solution of the equation.
item.dc:creator: Charles Bertucci (CEREMADE), Valentin Pesce (CMAP)

item.title: Almost Sure Convergence of Stochastic Approximation: An Interplay of Noise and Step Size
item.description: arXiv:2602.10580v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the almost sure convergence of the Stochastic Approximation algorithm to the fixed point $x^\star$ of a nonlinear operator under a negative drift condition and a general noise sequence with finite $p$-th moment for some $p > 1$. Classical almost sure convergence results of Stochastic Approximation are mostly analyzed for the square-integrable noise setting, and it is shown that any non-summable but square-summable step size sequence is sufficient to obtain almost sure convergence. However, such a limitation prevents wider algorithmic application. In particular, many applications in Machine Learning and Operations Research admit heavy-tailed noise with infinite variance, rendering such guarantees inapplicable. On the other hand, when a stronger condition on the noise is available, such guarantees on the step size would be too conservative, as practitioners would like to pick a larger step size for a more preferable convergence behavior. To this end, we show that any non-summable but $p$-th power summable step size sequence is sufficient to guarantee almost sure convergence, covering the gap in the literature. For the regime $p \in (1, 2)$, we show that using the $\|x-x^\star\|^p$-like Lyapunov function and applying the Holder-smoothness bound suffice. For $p > 2$, such an approach is no longer applicable, and therefore, we introduce a novel iterate projection technique to control the nonlinear terms produced by high-moment bounds and multiplicative noise. We believe our proof techniques and their implications could be of independent interest and pave the way for finite-time analysis of Stochastic Approximation under a general drift condition. As a starting point, we establish almost sure convergence results for non-expansive operators under a multiplicative noise condition for $p \in (1,2]$ and an additive noise condition for $p \in (2,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Hoang Huy Nguyen, Quang Dinh Thien Nguyen, Duc Anh Nguyen, Siva Theja Maguluri

item.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.08095v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}. In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^{\eta} \le C(d, \eta)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<\eta <1$.
item.dc:creator: Fan Chang, Joseph Slote, Chun-Kai Tseng, Alexander Volberg, Haonan Zhang

item.title: Wasserstein convergence rates for empirical measures of point processes
item.description: arXiv:2604.23928v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds on the convergence rate of empirical measures of point processes under the Wasserstein distance. To this end, we first introduce a new metric on the space of finite counting measures. Unlike many existing metrics in the literature, our proposed metric incorporates the spatial locations of unmatched points. Drawing on both this new metric and existing metrics from the literature, we identify a set of common structural properties and develop a general framework for Wasserstein distances between point-process distributions based on metrics satisfying these properties. We then use this framework to investigate the convergence rates of empirical measures, providing quantitative guarantees for approximating the distribution of the underlying point process, and further establish corresponding concentration inequalities. These theoretical results may provide ingredients for constructing oracle goodness-of-fit tests for a specified point-process distribution. We also apply our theory to the approximation of Campbell measures and discuss how the resulting bounds can help assess Wasserstein-based learning of generative point-process models.
item.dc:creator: Dongzhou Huang, Tianyi Jiang, Haonan Wang

item.title: Generalization of Zeroth-Order Method for Quotients of Quadratic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.26913v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimization of quadratic functions and their quotients is relevant in subspace and iterative optimization methods. In this paper, we consider the matrix-free computation of the generalized operator norm and the maximization of a generalized Rayleigh quotient when only forward evaluations of two linear operators $A$ and $B$ are available. The proposed method samples search directions uniformly from the full unit sphere, thereby avoiding tangent-space sampling and explicit access to the metric matrix $B^{\mathrm T}B$. The exact line search along each sampled direction reduces to a $2\times2$ generalized eigenvalue problem on specific Gram matrices. In the generic case its maximizing step has a closed form. We prove that the objective values converge almost surely to the largest generalized eigenvalue and that the distance of the iterates to the leading generalized eigenspace converges to zero. We also relate full-sphere moment estimators to the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. The numerical experiments on synthetic Gau{\ss}ian operators illustrate the behavior of the methods, and further studies of the proposed algorithms indicate favorable empirical convergence and weak dependence on the tested problem dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Bresch

item.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
item.description: arXiv:2605.08424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Piening, Richard Duong, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Sharp minimax risks and phase transitions in sparse submatrix detection
item.description: arXiv:2605.31583v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the minimax risk of detecting a sparse, elevated-mean Gaussian submatrix planted in a larger noisy matrix. When the planted submatrix has size $n\times n$ and the ambient matrix has size $N\times N$ with $N=n^{1+\alpha}$, the seminal work of Butucea and Ingster (2013) identifies the sharp detection boundary around which the risk converges to $0$ or $1$. We extend that zero-one theory by determining sharp risk asymptotics throughout a two-parameter phase diagram. Above the boundary, the risk decays stretched- or super-exponentially fast, and we determine its precise exponent. Below the boundary, where the risk tends to $1$, we obtain matching absolute-constant bounds for its polynomial rate of convergence. In both regimes, the asymptotics change across the line $\alpha+\delta=1/2$, where $\delta$ parametrizes the signed distance from the detection boundary. Finally, on the boundary, we show that the minimax risk converges to the nondegenerate constant $\frac12$ in a very sparse regime where $n$ remains fixed and $N\to\infty$. Each of these rates corresponds to the risk of a suitably calibrated scan or sum test, whence follow the upper bounds. The main problem is to derive the matching regime-specific lower bounds. The mixture likelihood ratio is an average rather than a product and thus its logarithm lacks the additive structure required by standard large deviation formulations. On the other hand, classical second-moment estimates fail to be sharp due to overlap-induced correlations. To address these issues, we develop two general lower-bound principles based on truncated mixture likelihoods, tailored to the target risks on both sides of the detection boundary. The same framework yields sharp risk asymptotics for sparse subtensors with equal side lengths and also applies to more general testing problems including the detection of rectangular subtensors.
item.dc:creator: Subhajit Goswami, Rajarshi Mukherjee

item.title: Determinantal sampling on general spaces: fast approximation via diffusion geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.06644v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) have recently emerged as a kernel-based alternative to standard independent sampling for constructing efficient minibatches, coresets, and other compact representations of large-scale datasets. One of the key strengths of DPP based samplers is that they can be deployed over very general spaces, in contrast to more classical sampling methods beyond i.i.d. which tend to be tailored to particular well-structured settings, principally Euclidean spaces. In this work, we establish explicit rate guarantees for determinantal sampling in spaces that extend far beyond known Euclidean setups, focussing on spectral kernels obtained from eigenspaces of naturally associated Markov diffusion operators, including in particular the Laplacian on manifolds and nearest-neighbour type graphs on data point clouds and the discrete Schrodinger operator on large scale networks. This covers, in particular, the settings of Riemannian manifolds and discrete networks, as well as the problem of batch sampling from discrete datasets. Overall, our approach achieves guarantees comparable to $\big(\text{sample size}\big)^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2d_{\text{int}}}}$ , which match with the rates for well-known determinantal samplers on Euclidean spaces of comparable dimension. In terms of techniques, we connect to the celebrated Weyl's Law for spectra on general spaces, and leverage tools from the theory of Markov diffusion operators and Dirichlet forms, which could be of independent interest in this area.
