Our approach is applicable to a very wide plethora of ambient spaces beyond Euclidean as soon as these ingredients are available, including e.g. fractals, leading to guarantees that will be governed by the intrinsic structural constants of such spaces.
item.dc:creator: Hoang-Son Tran, Pranav Gupta, Subhroshekhar Ghosh

item.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
item.description: arXiv:2607.17469v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $\nu$ satisfying $\nu[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the random tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth, a tree max-flow/min-cut identity that makes worst-case survival probabilities exact and optimizable over the algorithm's choices. Three applications follow. For $n$ tasks on one machine, each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set, every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-\Theta(n)]$; a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment that satisfies a majority of each clause, we determine the sharp source threshold $s_*$. Below $s_*$, on some instances a single admissible source forces nontermination however clauses are selected; at $s_*$, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial Hamming distance, against linear under independence, with matching worst-case instances; and any fixed margin above $s_*$ restores linear dependence on the distance. Third, verified backtracking for noisy predecessor search remains correct under a sufficiently strong bound on the comparison errors. In every setting the algorithm may also restart, which supplies no fresh randomness; restarting restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.
item.dc:creator: Yunbei Xu

item.title: A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.29429v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, for either a Steinhaus random multiplicative function or a Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)|\ll_{\varepsilon,f}\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}$. Together with Harper's almost sure lower bound, this determines the sharp logarithmic exponent in both models. This settles Harper's conjecture on the large fluctuations of random multiplicative functions.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Durkan, Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Exchangeable Testing Against an Unknown Benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2608.04838v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generate infinite binary exchangeable sequences by sequential comparison of data points against a latent benchmark. Assuming a prior distribution of the benchmark rank \(R_0\) within an unobserved group of players, we set up the Bayesian machinery which determines the posterior distribution of the running rank \(R_n\) in purely combinatorial terms, by counting insertion slots in a uniformly random ranking. This yields an explicit predictive probability of winning against the benchmark, which is a rational function of the counts. We identify some cases where the predictive probability has particularly simple form, notably a tournament related to the Topp--Leone distribution. The running benchmark rank is a P\'olya urn with random initial composition, and its normalised value converges to a latent strength variable with polynomial density. In a projective time scale, the fluctuations of the normalised rank about this limit are Brownian, with the Wright--Fisher coefficient frozen at the limit, while the associated recurrent up-down Markov chain on a high level $n$ of the Pascal graph is approximated by a Wright--Fisher diffusion with a nonlinear drift expressed through the prior density.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Gnedin

item.title: The Tamed Subgradient Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm beyond Convexity
item.description: arXiv:2608.06283v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of sampling from target distributions whose potentials are simultaneously non-smooth, subject to superlinear gradient growth, and non-convex. We introduce the Subgradient Tamed Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (SG-TULA), a discretisation of the Langevin diffusion that operates directly on subgradients, without relying on computationally demanding smoothing procedures. To handle the superlinear regime, taming techniques are employed to produce a stable, explicit scheme. We derive non-asymptotic convergence bounds in Wasserstein-2 distance, with all constants tracked explicitly in terms of dimension and inverse temperature, improving upon the currently known rates for subgradient-based Langevin algorithms. We further provide excess risk estimates for the associated optimisation problem. We verify the assumptions, with explicit constants, for the regularized pretraining potential of a LLM in the GPT-2 lineage and the boosted coordinate-wise variant of SG-TULA pretrains the former competitively against finetuned AdamW and Muon, for which no comparable non-asymptotic guarantees are presently available.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Lytras, Nikolaos Makras, Sotirios Sabanis

item.title: Turning angle analysis reveals hidden anisotropies in intracellular transport
item.description: arXiv:2608.07975v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Molecular motion within living cells provides a window into the physical principles underlying intracellular organization and transport. Yet a fundamental limitation remains: measured trajectories are often short, noisy, and randomly oriented, rendering spatial anisotropies inaccessible to conventional analyses. We show that turning-angle statistics provide a robust approach for uncovering anisotropies in anomalous diffusion. Using a two-dimensional anisotropic fractional Brownian motion model with random orientations, we show theoretically and through simulations that turning-angle distributions preserve signatures of anisotropy. We apply this approach to single-particle tracking data, including quantum dots in the cytoplasm of HeLa cells and membrane proteins in hippocampal neurons. Turning angles reveal hidden anisotropies in the motion of quantum dots and Kv1.4 channels, and in specific dynamical states of glycoprotein CD4. These results establish turning-angle analysis as a powerful strategy for detecting organization in complex environments and reveal that anisotropic anomalous diffusion is an {often} overlooked feature of intracellular dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Balcerek, Adrian Pacheco-Pozo, Agnieszka Wy{\l}oma\'nska, Diego Krapf

item.title: From Truncation to Commitment: Persistent Context in Uniform Discrete Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2609.01043v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Uniform-state discrete diffusion models update all tokens in parallel while keeping every position revisable. Even when the commonly used top-$p$ rule leaves only one candidate at a position, that choice affects only the current reverse step and can be revised at the next sampling step. We ask what changes when selected hypotheses instead become persistent context for later predictions. We therefore propose committed reveal sampling (CRS), a training-free sampler that stores selected argmax tokens and inserts them into subsequent model inputs. Our analysis separates persistent context from truncation. Within one reverse step, adaptive top-$p$, randomized or not, reproduces the update induced by a visible token only when a likelihood-ratio ordering holds, while in a simple latent-mode model, keeping the selected token visible helps later parallel predictions agree on the same sequence-level choice. Empirically, paired experiments on Duo-distilled then separate this persistent effect from single-step top-$p$ restriction and scalar temperature scaling. Under the same finalization rule, CRS without top-$p$ truncation reaches lower generative perplexity (GenPPL) than fixed $p=0.95$ and $p=0.9$ baselines across budgets of 8--64 function evaluations (NFE). At 64 NFE, the comparison at matched unigram entropy also gives lower GenPPL for CRS, shifting the GenPPL--entropy tradeoff under this metric. Base Duo shows the same direction in a descriptive comparison, while other diversity and continuation metrics can rank these operating points differently. A distributional distance to held-out text (SOL) under a fixed GPT-2-Large representation also decreases with persistent context at the same late top-$p$ threshold. These results identify support restriction and persistent context as distinct controls of that tradeoff.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Hayakawa

item.title: The norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator
item.description: arXiv:2609.12440v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the exact $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator for every $1<p<\infty$, proving that it equals $p/(p-1)$. This settles the sharp strong-type problem for the centered maximal operator on the real line. For every $p$ in this range, the norm is strictly larger than the constant associated with the critical power $|x|^{-1/p}$, thereby disproving the conjecture of Dror, Ganguli, and Strichartz that this profile determines the unrestricted norm.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: Strong laws, random monotone vector fields and gradient flows on metric spaces of nonpositive curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.16439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a probabilistic Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for the gradient flow generated by an integral function over suitable separable Hadamard spaces. This result leverages Stojkovi\'c's Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for gradient flows of sums of convex functions and Ba\v{c}\'ak's result relating resolvent and gradient flow convergence, along with a strong law of large numbers for normal convex integrands. For separable Hilbert spaces and locally compact Hadamard spaces, these strong laws follow from results of King and Wets and Artstein and Wets, respectively, but we crucially go beyond these examples by establishing a new such strong law for normal convex integrands on all Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones are isometric to Hilbert spaces, a class that includes non-Hilbertian, non-locally compact examples such as infinite-dimensional hyperbolic space. This new strong law arises as a combination of a strong law of large numbers for integrable random monotone vector fields on Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, that is, Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones all embed isometrically into Hilbert spaces, extending a result of Salim from Hilbert spaces, together with a new result on the interchangeability of the subdifferential and the integral, which we establish for $L^2$-Lipschitz integrands. This latter ingredient provides, to our knowledge, the first nonlinear version of (a particular case of) a previous result due variously to Ioffe and Tikhomirov, Levin, Hiriart-Urruty, Thibault as well as Rockafellar and Wets. On the way to this strong law for random monotone vector fields, we also establish a distribution-uniform generalization of Sturm's strong law of large numbers for inductive means of $L^1$-sequences of i.i.d. random variables on Hadamard spaces via a new effective non-asymptotic concentration inequality. Throughout the paper, we highlight various remaining open problems.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Pischke
